title: WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.5 -> 0.7 (longer LR decay)
description: One constant: WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.5 -> 0.7 at the unmodified depth-10 / HEAD_DIM 128 baseline; LR plateau ends at 30% of the budget instead of 50%, time-average lrm 0.75 -> 0.65. Nothing else changed.
reflection: val_bpb 0.987227 vs the 0.988076 baseline: -0.00085, i.e. a marginal win at best and I will not call it a confirmed one. It is ~1.8 sigma on the pooled 4.8e-4 floor and inside the ~1-2e-3 floor a1 argues for (#108), so a single run cannot separate it from noise. The change is exactly free in throughput, which makes it a clean read: 1121 steps vs the baseline's 1119, 293.9M tokens vs 293.3M, MFU 42.03% vs 41.94%, 34.6GB, 85.9M params. Any delta is the schedule alone. The interesting detail is that train and val moved in OPPOSITE directions: final smoothed train loss 2.765 vs the baseline's 2.752, so the model fit the training data slightly WORSE and generalised slightly better. Every other result in this cell had train and val ordered together (HD64: 2.788 train / 0.9953 val; MATRIX_LR up: 2.806-2.817 train / worse val), so the mechanism here is different in kind - lowering the LR integral is trading fit for generalisation, not simply optimising better or worse. That is a real effect signature rather than a noise signature, but the magnitude is small and it does not license a claim. Practical reading for the cell: the schedule axis is REAL BUT SHALLOW on this side. a3's 0.5 -> 0.3 cost +0.0056 against its matched control while 0.5 -> 0.7 buys only -0.0009, so the curve is steeply bad below 0.5 and nearly flat above it - the baseline sat just inside the plateau, not far from the optimum. Nobody should expect a large win from 0.85; whoever ran it will most likely report another sub-noise number, and if it does land near -0.001 too then the honest group conclusion is that 0.7-0.85 is a ~0.001 plateau and the schedule axis should be closed. The broader lesson from my three rounds: every knob at fixed model size has now produced effects of order 0.001-0.007, while the one big move in the cell (-0.0093) was a shape change. With 17 runs left, hunting further 0.001s one constant at a time is a losing allocation.
